note: Block 9 step 4. Every model format that declares companions must answer every negative case, or say why the case cannot apply to it. A cell is `covered-by-existing` when a slice already proved it (the test is named so the claim is checkable), `added` when step 4 wrote it, and `not-applicable` only with a reason that is a fact about the format or the codec, never a plan.

sharedResolverNote: The host resolver is one implementation shared by every format, so the cases that are properties of resolution rather than of a file — patterns, budgets, cancellation, case folding, teardown — are proved once against a fake origin backend and hold for all four formats. Those cells point at that suite instead of repeating it four times.

missing-required-companion.reason: VXL declares exactly one requirement and it is optional: a voxel model without its .hva is a complete voxel model, so the format has no required companion to lose.

missing-optional-companion.test: opens without a sidecar and says the capability is simply absent

invalid-companion-magic.test: VXL refuses an HVA whose header is not an HVA header

truncated-input.test: keeps the model readable when the sidecar is truncated, and names the damage

duplicate-or-ambiguous-candidates.test: VXL refuses two sidecars that both answer the declared name

traversal-or-absolute-reference.note: VXL derives its pattern from its own subject identity, not from file content, so there is no content-derived reference to poison; the host refuses hostile candidate ids for every backend.

case-collision.test: folds case on an insensitive backend, so two spellings are one companion

complete-companion-set.test: declares the exact texture the model names and binds it from the sibling directory

missing-required-companion.reason: W3D declares only optional texture companions: Command & Conquer 3 ships its models in Misc.big and its textures in Terrain.big, so a model whose textures are unreachable is a complete model and must still open.

missing-optional-companion.test: opens with the texture missing and reports it as unbound

invalid-companion-magic.reason: The W3D codec binds texture bytes and never decodes them, so it has no magic to check; a corrupt DDS is the image codec's problem when that subject is opened, not this one's.

truncated-input.test: refuses a chunk whose declared size runs past its parent

traversal-or-absolute-reference.test: W3D refuses a texture name that is a path

sage-w3x.label: SAGE W3X (+ skeleton and texture companions)

complete-companion-set.test: names bones from the bound skeleton and marks them as companion facts

missing-required-companion.reason: Both W3X requirements are optional: a mesh opened on its own is a complete mesh, and the skeleton only adds bone names, so the format declares nothing it must have.

missing-optional-companion.test: leaves a bone unnamed when no hierarchy is reachable, instead of borrowing the part id

invalid-companion-magic.test: W3X ignores a bound skeleton that is not a W3X document

truncated-input.test: W3X refuses a document truncated mid-element

duplicate-or-ambiguous-candidates.test: W3X refuses two skeletons that both answer the declared id

traversal-or-absolute-reference.test: refuses a hierarchy reference that is %s

case-collision.test: folds case on an insensitive backend, so two spellings are one companion

budget-exceeded.test: stops enumerating at its entry limit instead of walking a large directory

cancellation.test: cancels in the middle of an enumeration and leaves nothing open

protected-or-unknown-tail.test: reports tags it does not decode instead of dropping them silently

complete-companion-set.test: binds a texture the model names, out of the same archive, through current-mount

missing-required-companion.reason: M3 declares only optional texture companions: StarCraft II files a model and its textures under different mod roots of one merged namespace, so an unbound texture is the normal shipped case.

missing-optional-companion.test: opens from a plain directory with the path-shaped reference unbound

invalid-companion-magic.reason: The M3 codec binds texture bytes and never decodes them, so it has no magic to check; validating a DDS belongs to the image codec that opens it as its own subject.

truncated-input.test: M3 refuses a section index that runs past the file

duplicate-or-ambiguous-candidates.test: binds a texture the model names, out of the same archive, through current-mount
duplicate-or-ambiguous-candidates.note: The same test carries the decoy: a second .dds beside the named one is never bound, because the declaration is an exact path rather than an extension.

case-collision.test: folds case on an insensitive backend, so two spellings are one companion

budget-exceeded.test: refuses a name-only requirement over a namespace too large to scan
budget-exceeded.note: Measured on the installed StarCraft II CASC: 666,588 entries, refused by budget rather than scanned.

cancellation.test: cancels in the middle of an enumeration and leaves nothing open

protected-or-unknown-tail.reason: The M3 codec claims no byte-preservation contract: it publishes the section index and does not rewrite the file, so there is no protected tail it could drop. Section tags it does not decode are already listed in `sectionTags`.

teardown-after-failure.test: holds the container while the child lives and gives it back on dispose

crossCutting.test: no failure path leaks an absolute local path into a diagnostic
